pickOne: Choose a file to read or edit it.

columns.name: Site
form.name: Name (lowercase letters, digits, dashes)
form.nameTaken: A router or service with this name already exists in another file. Saving will be refused.
managed.none: No site built with the form yet.
managed.byHand: edited by hand: change it in the files view
followUp.title: Your new site
followUp.created: The site is saved and Traefik will serve it. Two things remain: the DNS name must point to this node, and (with HTTPS) Traefik must get the certificate.
followUp.certHint: The certificate is requested by Traefik once the name resolves. This page checks again every few seconds.
middlewares.title: Middlewares
middlewares.explain: Ready-made protections and tweaks you attach to a site: only your network, a password, security headers… Pick what you want; the file is written for you.
middlewares.byHand: edited by hand: change the file instead
middlewares.inUse: Detach it from the sites that use it first
middlewares.confirmDelete: Delete this middleware? Its text stays in the file history.
middlewares.name: Name
middlewares.hashed: Passwords are hashed here (bcrypt) and only the hash is written. They are never shown again.
middlewares.frameDeny: Forbid showing the site in a frame
coherence.explain: Checks that your configuration files agree with each other. Nothing is changed. References to things Traefik creates elsewhere (Docker labels, its own internals) cannot be checked and are not blamed.
coherence.truncated: There are more files than could be read: the check is incomplete.
coherence.unreadable: {{path}} cannot be read as YAML and was left out of the check.
coherence.codes.duplicate.router: also defined in {{detail}}: Traefik keeps only one of them.
coherence.codes.duplicate.service: also defined in {{detail}}: Traefik keeps only one of them.
coherence.codes.duplicate.middleware: also defined in {{detail}}: Traefik keeps only one of them.
coherence.codes.router.no_rule: this router has no rule, so it matches nothing.
coherence.codes.router.no_service: this router has no service to send traffic to.
coherence.codes.router.service_missing: its service {{detail}} does not exist in the files.
coherence.codes.router.middleware_missin: its middleware {{detail}} does not exist in the files.
coherence.codes.chain.middleware_missing: this chain uses {{detail}}, which does not exist.
coherence.codes.chain.loop: this chain leads back to itself: {{detail}}.
coherence.codes.router.duplicate_rule: same rule and entry points as {{detail}}: only one of them gets the traffic.
middlewares.renameSites: {{count}} site(s) built with the form will follow the new name: {{sites}}.
middlewares.renameManual: These files name the middleware and are never rewritten for you. Change them by hand, or the sites in them will lose it: {{files}}.
domain.title: Pause a whole domain
domain.hint: Stops serving every site whose addresses all belong to the domain. The DNS is not touched, and nothing is deleted.
domain.name: Domain (for example example.com)
domain.none: No site to change for this domain.
domain.shared: Left alone because they also answer for another domain: {{sites}}.
static.title: Static configuration
static.notConfigured: This node has no static configuration folder set up. Mount the folder that holds traefik.yml for the worker and set ARMADOK_TRAEFIK_STATIC_DIR (see the worker example file).
static.explain: Entry points, certificate resolvers, the API, logs and metrics. Traefik reads this file only when it starts: a change counts after a restart. Each replaced version is kept on the node. YAML anchors and aliases are not accepted.
static.tooLong: The file is too long to compare here. You can still save it.
static.saved: Saved. Traefik keeps running with the old file until it restarts.
static.confirmRestart: Restarting Traefik interrupts every site for a few seconds. Continue?
block.name: Name
block.nameHelp: The name of the file Armadok writes for this site. It cannot be changed afterwards.
block.whenHelp: The addresses this site answers to. Any one of them is enough (OR). A path condition must also match (AND).
block.applyHelp: Middlewares run in the order shown, from first to last: for example a login before a header.
block.sendHelp: Where the request goes once it has passed the blocks above.
block.httpsHelp: Serve the site over HTTPS. Traefik obtains the certificate with the resolver you name.
form.noMiddleware: Nothing is applied: visitors go straight to the site.
viewHints.sites: What the configuration files define, read-only
viewHints.managed: Sites you create and edit from Armadok
viewHints.middlewares: Reusable steps applied to requests: redirects, authentication, headers…
viewHints.coherence: Finds sites pointing nowhere, missing middlewares, unused services
viewHints.static: Traefik's start-up settings (entry points, resolvers, logs)
managed.newTip: Opens the site builder: address, destination, security
managed.pauseTip: Takes the site offline without deleting it; resume it any time.
managed.historyTip: Earlier versions of this site, to put one back
